observations.observation: As prior context, Micron's June 24 Q3 remarks already expected tight supply conditions to persist beyond calendar 2027, citing AI demand and structural supply constraints.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This establishes an existing tight-supply baseline; it does not quantify realized shortages or prove future conditions.

observations.observation: In September 30 Q4 prepared remarks, Micron projected tighter memory and storage supply-demand conditions in calendar 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, while expecting DRAM and NAND shipments to grow and remaining supply-constrained. Micron said it had no line of sight to when supply and demand would balance.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are management forecasts, not observed 2027–28 outcomes; the remarks also project industry bit-shipment growth.

observations.observation: The official release reports Q4 actual gross margin of 86.8% GAAP and 87.0% non-GAAP. The 86.25% figure is Q1 FY2027 guidance, alongside revenue guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion and EPS guidance of $38.15 plus or minus $1.00.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The supplied article's opening characterization of 86.25% as a record gross margin can be confused with the actual Q4 result; its later text describes the figure as a forecast.

observations.observation: The Micron financial call was scheduled for September 30 at 4:30 p.m. ET. The earliest independent report located in search metadata was PC Gamer at 10:13:59Z on October 1; the supplied Tom's Hardware article followed at 12:50Z and was captured at 12:52:28Z, before cutoff.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: PC Gamer's timestamp is from search metadata and no dated pre-cutoff page snapshot was obtained; it is the earliest located coverage, not necessarily the earliest public report. Exact posting time of Micron's release and prepared remarks is not available.

observations.observation: A pre-event Tom's Hardware report attributed to Acer CEO Jason Chen a more optimistic PC-price forecast: near-term rises, a plateau in the first half of 2027, and potential declines later in 2027 with Chinese capacity.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is an Acer executive's forecast as reported by Tom's Hardware, and concerns PC-component pricing rather than a direct measurement of DRAM/NAND industry supply or Micron's committed capacity.

gaps: No pre-cutoff full transcript with an original, dated snapshot was verified. The statement that most overall capacity was already sold is available in contemporaneous reporting; Micron's dated prepared remarks more narrowly confirm agreements covering the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bit supply and higher year-over-year pricing.
Exact posting times for Micron's September 30 release and prepared remarks are not shown; only the date and call time are verified.
The Acer counterpoint is secondary reporting; the original DigiTimes interview or transcript was not independently verified.
The sources concern memory-industry forecasts and do not establish a specific Intel supplier allocation, order, shipment, or cost impact by cutoff.
research_notes: Cutoff: 2026-10-01T12:55:24.579038Z.
